title: How can sticks add, subtract, multiply and divide?
description: Two piles of sticks are added, subtracted, multiplied and divided using only joining, pairing, repeating and grouping, with no number names. The video uses the same stick-by-stick pairing as the example in the book, then puts the answers back to check them.
teaching_notes: One idea: when numbers are sticks, each operation is something we do to piles. Pairing stick by stick shows what is left over when one pile is taken from another. Watch for students who reach for number names, which the question does not allow.

source: Figure it Out (the mechanism of counting, question 1)
video_script.why: The child shows that the four operations come from simple actions on piles of sticks, using the same stick-by-stick pairing as the solved example.
video_script.substitution: Draw two piles of sticks and act on them: join, pair and remove, repeat, take out groups.
video_script.anchor: two piles of sticks, a first pile and a second pile, drawn side by side
video_script.payoff_line: Joining, pairing, repeating and grouping do all four jobs

final_answer.value: Add by joining; subtract by pairing and removing; multiply by repeating one pile for every stick of the other; divide by taking out equal groups
final_answer.spoken: add by joining, subtract by pairing and removing, multiply by repeating one pile for every stick of the other, and divide by taking out equal groups

hold_back: Add by joining; subtract by pairing and removing; multiply by repeating one pile for every stick of the other; divide by taking out equal groups
never_show: any numeral or number name for a pile
the answer card before the last beat of the board solution
maths_rules: adding: put the two piles together; the joined pile is the sum
subtracting: pair sticks of the smaller pile with sticks of the larger pile, stick by stick, and take the pairs away; the unpaired sticks are what is left
multiplying: lay out the first pile once for every stick of the second pile and join all the copies
dividing: keep taking out a group the size of the second pile from the first; the number of groups is the answer and sticks that cannot fill a group are the leftover
check: the unpaired sticks joined to the smaller pile give back the larger pile; the groups taken out, put back, give the first pile again
video_script.design: One idea: each operation is an action on piles of sticks. The two piles stay on the stage and each step acts on them. No numeral or number name is used.
